newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Products Outlook-gasoline supplies seen ample.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Products Outlook-gasoline supplies seen ample.

text.p: Gasoline buyers are expected to step back from the market early this week, with traders seeing some further downside potential for spot prices East of the Rockies due to ample supplies.
Market talk that Citgo's 65,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at its Corpus Christi refinery restarted over the weekend should contribute to that bearishness, traders said.
"There's a lot of people waiting to buy gasoline, but they'll probably wait until the (extra barrels) come back on," one trader said.
"All in all, the market's pretty balanced (between supply and demand) right now," the trader added.
Talk last week of problems at several refineries -- speculation, based on some aggressive buying by the companies concerned -- failed to generate strength in the gasoline market, traders said.

There is a continued lack of buying interest from players generally, despite the latest American Petroleum Institute figures which put gasoline stocks at 194 million barrels, nearly 9.7 million barrels below the year-ago level with the most notable shortfall of reformulated gasoline in New York Harbor (PADD I).

Traders continued to point to the restart of Tosco's Trainer refinery in Pennsylvania as the key factor keeping a lid on gasoline prices. That refinery is expected to return near mid-month and operate at about 150,000 bpd by the end of May. Approxiamately 100,000 bpd of gasoline output is expected from the facility, which was shuttered in December 1995 ahead of its sale to Tosco.

"One of the barometers is going to be whether or when the Tosco plant comes up," said Paulo Nery, senior consultant with the Houston-based Pace Consultants Inc. "If they come out smoothly then prices are going to soften up," he added.
In addition, the steady stream of gasoline and gasoline blendstocks coming from Europe and South America should continue in the near-term.
"I dont see a lot of movement in gasoline because of the imports coming in," Nery said.
In the nation's midcontinent markets appeared to be well-balanced, with stocks adequate and prices lacking any definitive trend.
"I don't see any evidence of tightness in any product," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil in Chicago.

But some traders continued to express concern that delays on Explorer Pipeline due to maintenance last month on the Houston-to-Tulsa-to-Chicago refined products line might boost gasoline values ahead of the U.S. Memorial Day holiday.
Gasoline demand historically starts to plateau in the U.S. at that three-day weekend at the end of May, and continues through the U.S. Labor Day holiday in early September.

On the West Coast, traders said gasoline was likely to remain under pressure following the 1.4 million barrel build in stocks shown in last week's API report, putting the overall level at 28.1 million barrels.

West Coast CARB diesel fuel prices should also see further bearish sentiment after reports last week that ARCO may have a damaged processor at its Los Angeles refinery, creating backups and pressuring prices.
